entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9827"/><div sID="gen17401" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9827"/><hi type="bold">8. altogether--</hi>rather, "all alike" [Maurer]. Even the so-called "wise" men (<reference osisRef="Jer.10.7">Jr 10:7</reference>) of the Gentiles are on a level with the brutes and "foolish," namely, because they connive at the popular idolatry (compare <reference osisRef="Rom.1.21-Rom.1.28">Ro 1:21-28</reference>). Therefore, in Daniel and Revelation, the world power is represented under a bestial form. Man divests himself of his true humanity, and sinks to the level of the brute, when he severs his connection with God (<reference osisRef="Ps.115.8">Psa 115:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jonah.2.8">Jon 2:8</reference>).<div eID="gen17401" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17402" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stock is a doctrine of vanities--</hi>The stock (put for the worship of all idols whatever, made out of a stock) speaks for itself that the whole theory of idolatry is vanity (<reference osisRef="Isa.44.9-Isa.44.11">Is 44:9-11</reference>). Castalio translates, "the very wood itself confuting the vanity" (of the idol). <div eID="gen17402" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9828"/><div sID="gen17403" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9828"/>9. Everything connected with idols is the result of human effort.<div eID="gen17403" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17404" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Silver spread--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Isa.30.22">Is 30:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.40.19">Is 40:19</reference>).<div eID="gen17404" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17405" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Tarshish--</hi>Tartessus, in Spain, famed for precious metals.<div eID="gen17405" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17406" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Uphaz--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Dan.10.5">Da 10:5</reference>). As the Septuagint in the Syrian Hexapla in the Margin, Theodotus, the Syrian and Chaldee versions have "Ophir," Gesenius thinks "Uphaz" a colloquial corruption (one letter only being changed) for "Ophir." Heeren thinks Ophir the general name for the rich countries of the south, on the Arabian, African, and Indian coasts; just as our term, East Indies.<div eID="gen17406" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17407" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cunning--</hi>skilful. <div eID="gen17407" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9829"/><div sID="gen17408" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9829"/><hi type="bold">10. true God--</hi>literally, "God Jehovah is truth"; not merely true, that is, veracious, but truth in the reality of His essence, as opposed to the "vanity" or emptiness which all idols are (<reference osisRef="Jer.10.3">Jr 10:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.8.15">8, 15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.15.3">2Ch 15:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.31.5">Psa 31:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1John.5.20">1Jo 5:20</reference>).<div eID="gen17408" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17409" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">living God--</hi>(<reference osisRef="John.5.26">Joh 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Tim.6.17">1Ti 6:17</reference>). He hath life in Himself which no creature has. All else "live in Him" (<reference osisRef="Acts.17.28">Ac 17:28</reference>). In contrast to dead idols.<div eID="gen17409" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17410" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">everlasting--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.10.16">Psa 10:16</reference>). In contrast to the temporary existence of all other objects of worship. <div eID="gen17410" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9830"/><div sID="gen17411" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9830"/>11. This verse is in Chaldee, Jeremiah supplying his countrymen with a formula of reply to Chaldee idolaters in the tongue most intelligible to the latter. There may be also derision intended in imitating their barbarous dialect. Rosenmuller objects to this view, that not merely the words put in the mouths of the Israelites, but Jeremiah's own introductory words, "Thus shall ye say to them," are in Chaldee, and thinks it to be a marginal gloss. But it is found in all the oldest versions. It was an old Greek saying: "Whoever thinks himself a god besides the one God, let him make another world" (<reference osisRef="Ps.96.5">Psa 96:5</reference>).<div eID="gen17411" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17412" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall perish--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.2.18">Is 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.13.2">Zec 13:2</reference>).<div eID="gen17412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17413" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">these heavens--</hi>the speaker pointing to them with his fingers. <div eID="gen17413" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9835"/><div sID="gen17422" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9835"/><hi type="bold">16. portion--</hi>from a Hebrew root, "to divide." God is the all-sufficient Good of His people (<reference osisRef="Num.18.20">Nu 18:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.16.5">Psa 16:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.73.26">73:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.3.24">La 3:24</reference>).<div eID="gen17422" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17423" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not like them--</hi>not like the idols, a vain object of trust (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.31">De 32:31</reference>).<div eID="gen17423" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17424" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">former of all things--</hi>the Fashioner (as a potter, <reference osisRef="Isa.64.8">Is 64:8</reference>) of the universe.<div eID="gen17424" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17425" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rod of his inheritance--</hi>The portion marked off as His inheritance by the measuring rod (<reference osisRef="Ezek.48.21">Eze 48:21</reference>). As He is their portion, so are they His portion (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.9">De 32:9</reference>). A reciprocal tie (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.51.19">Jr 51:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.74.2">Psa 74:2</reference>, Margin).
